anchor_definition: The anchor is the login submit handler recorded as the answer in 1.json (label controllers.js:345 -> the doLogin@329 body). It reads the credentials, base64-encodes the password (password: base64Encode(password)) and assembles + sends the POST /login whose password field is the observed token. The construction path is graded below it: loginService.login (the dedicated /login request builder, 0.7) -> base64Encode (generic base64 primitive that produces the token bytes, 0.5) -> $iq_http.http (generic ajax transport/sink, 0.2). base64Decode is the off-chain inverse; the three sibling doLogin handlers (different login flows) are off-chain lookalike decoys. NOTE: controllers.js holds four near-identical $scope.doLogin handlers; the anchor is specifically the one at offset 8780 (line 329) that drives the captured loginService.login request — pinned by explicit offsets because the four share an identical header.

primary_anchor.why: $scope.doLogin@329, the login handler captured as the 1.json answer: it reads username/password, base64-encodes the password (password: base64Encode(password)), assembles the request data and calls loginService.login -> the POST /login whose password field is the observed base64 token. This is the specific handler matching the captured request, distinct from the three sibling doLogin flows.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span (file + offsets + sha256 of one complete function).

A returned function name is scored against answer_function ONLY when that identifier is recoverable from the captured slice (named declaration, leading property key, or leading `NAME =`). Anonymous function expressions are graded by span alone.
Explanation must distinguish the anchor from the call-site wrapper, the generic crypto primitive, the sink and same-request decoy fields.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function.

role_oracle.why: $scope.doLogin@329, the login handler captured as the 1.json answer: it reads username/password, base64-encodes the password (password: base64Encode(password)), assembles the request data and calls loginService.login -> the POST /login whose password field is the observed base64 token. This is the specific handler matching the captured request, distinct from the three sibling doLogin flows.

loginService.login (service.js): the dedicated /login request builder. It assembles the POST params for the login endpoint (url = server()+'login', method POST) carrying the credential payload with the base64 password, then hands them to the generic transport. A target-specific helper nested below the submit handler and above the generic ajax transport.

A generic, keyless base64 encoder (out += base64EncodeChars.charAt(...)) that encodes any string. It computes the observed token bytes but is not bound to the password field — doLogin binds it. Reusable encoding primitive shared across login/register flows; a Core utility below the target-specific request builder.

$iq_http.http (app.min.js): the generic angular $http transport wrapper used by every service method (login, register, validate, ...). It emits the already-built request and returns the promise — the generic ajax sender/sink, not login-specific.
The inverse base64 decoder defined next to base64Encode; never on the password-encoding path. A pure decoy.

Sibling $scope.doLogin@799: a near-identical login handler in a different controller/flow (it base64-encodes the password but drives a different login service call, not the captured POST /login). A strong lookalike decoy, not the handler that produced the observed request.
Sibling $scope.doLogin@1484: a near-identical login handler in a different controller/flow. A strong lookalike decoy, not the captured-request handler.
Sibling $scope.doLogin@1893: a near-identical login handler in a different controller/flow. A strong lookalike decoy, not the captured-request handler.

scoring_policy.source_level_answer: not_applicable_for_real_captures; grade by captured_span and answer_function only
scoring_policy.anonymous_anchor_name: when answer_function is not recoverable from the captured slice, the name veto is skipped and an exact/unique span match scores the role regardless of submitted name
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span

do_not_promote: The network sink / request-sending service emits an already constructed value and is not the constructor.
Thin forwarding wrappers and submit handlers that merely call the value constructor should not outrank the anchor.
Generic crypto/encoding primitives (md5/AES/RSA/SM/base64/uuid libraries) are Core utilities, below the field-binding anchor.
Same-request OTHER fields (a second encrypted parameter, signatures, fingerprints) are off-chain decoys for this observable.
oracle_notes.offset_convention: All offsets are 0-based UTF-16 code-unit indices over the BOM-stripped UTF-8 text. sha256 is over the UTF-8 bytes of the slice. This differs from the synthetic suite's response_schema wording ("byte offset"); both graders slice by their own convention.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Span maps uniquely to primary_anchor.captured_span (the field-binding/value-constructing function).
Span maps to a target-specific helper nested below the anchor.
Span maps to a generic crypto/encoding primitive used by the construction path.
Span maps to a path-critical step, a forwarding wrapper or the submit handler.
Span maps to a generic low-level helper (BigInt math, DOM read) on the upstream path.
Span maps to an off-chain decoy / same-request other field, or cannot be uniquely mapped.
